domain: emergency response / per-incident and per-exposure register
prediction_question: OPEN - to be fixed by the field-list probe before this can advance. Two candidate framings: (a) sibling framing, NOT differentiated on its own: for an emergency incident dispatched to FENZ, will the first-appliance arrival exceed a fixed response-time threshold (the published austin-911-response candidate, US, is exactly this task family for police calls - a FENZ version would need a stated substantive difference beyond jurisdiction); (b) distinctive framing, preferred for novelty: for a fire/vegetation-fire incident given what is known at dispatch or at first report, will the incident develop additional property exposures (one record per exposure; an incident with >1 exposure means the hazard spread to another building/location)? The metadata field list decides which framings the source can carry.
prediction_time: OPEN - depends on the framing fixed by the field-list probe. Framing (b) would use the dispatch/first-report instant: incident type as called in, time of day, season, location (region/station-area), and whatever pre-attendance fields the CAD (ICAD) record carries at that moment; every Station Management System field completed after attendance is post-instant and must not ship.
target_definition: OPEN - framing (b): binary per-incident additional-exposure occurrence derived from the exposure grain (the publisher states one record per exposure; an incident is a single episode that can contain multiple exposures). Source column: the incident/exposure identifier pair; excludable from shipped features by construction.

next_action: The cheapest unresolved fact is the field list, because it decides which prediction task this source can carry at all. Next probe, in order: (1) read FENZ Incident Metadata 2026_01.pdf cleanly - try (a) a plain fetch from a worker (tests both the bot wall and the bulk path in one probe) and (b) a fresh browser-session download if (a) is blocked; enumerate every timestamp field (call received, dispatch, arrival), the pre-attendance CAD fields, the post-attendance SMS fields, and the exposure/incident identifier pair; (2) with the field list, fix the target: prefer the exposure-formation framing (b) unless the timestamps for it are post-dispatch completions; a response-time target requires a written differentiation against the published austin-911-response candidate (US police calls) beyond jurisdiction; (3) measure per-year incident and exposure counts and the multi-exposure base rate from one annual TSV (bounded, 67-75 MB, worker-side); (4) run check-novelty.py once the target is fixed. Do not spend further probes before (1) - everything downstream depends on it.
